content.comment_body: What is [product_name] [version_no]? Where can it be found? I have two manuals for the [product_name] Communication Interface Module: [document] 08/2022, [article_no] and [document] 03/2023, [article_no] [document] - [product_name] - ID: [article_no] - Industry Support [company_name] “[version_no] provides the following new features:…” My main question: what is [version_no]? Is this firmware, software, or hardware? After reviewing the manual, it appears to be a new firmware version. Next, where is it available? I’ve searched through the forum, the [company_name] website, and the internet, but haven’t found it. Using the link provided in the manual yields no results. Does [version_no] actually exist, or is it something [company_name] was planning but hasn't released yet? Can anyone help locate it?

It's common for [company_name] to publish manuals for new device versions before official release. In my location (Germany), even the latest manual isn't listed on the support pages yet. Clicking the shared link brings up the German version of the manual. This is something only [company_name] can answer, not the forum members.

The answer is: 3-31-2023 > "Good morning, There is a new firmware update, [version_no], for the [product_name] module; however, it has not been released yet. We are reaching out to the product manager to get an update on when the firmware will be available. We'll inform you once we have a reply from the product manager. Best regards, [company_name] Technical Support" However, based on previous experiences: When the [product_name] Mobile Communication Module was announced, I checked about North American market availability. Initially told it would take about a year, later updates were inconclusive, and even after several years, it remained unavailable. Later, when the [product_name] Interface Module was finally launched, I obtained one of the first units for North America. It features a four-port switch, although it lost several functions compared to the previous module. I set it aside for some time before deciding to learn how to use it. A single global cellular engine in the old module might have been simpler, but [company_name] seems to have had other reasons for the current approach.

UPDATE: On 4/3/2023, [company_name] Support wrote: "Good morning, According to the product manager, the firmware update [version_no] has not been released and there is no set release date. We have been informed it may come out in a few weeks, but nothing is confirmed. Best regards, [company_name] Technical Support"

Just to clarify: [product_name] [version_no] hardware is now available. With this version, SGLAN functionality is supported. Older [product_name] hardware with previous versions cannot be upgraded to [version_no], as it is a new hardware release.

analysis.insight_summary: Users reported confusion after [company_name] published manuals mentioning new features for [product_name] [version_no] before its release. Several users struggled to locate or confirm availability, while official support responses acknowledged delays and lack of clear release timelines. It was eventually clarified that [version_no] refers to a new hardware module—not firmware—and older hardware cannot be upgraded, which heightened users’ frustration regarding unclear documentation and unpredictable product availability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward, timely, and precise information about the status, characteristics, and access to new [product_name] versions referenced in official manuals.
